questions.q: In SELECT Name, Account.Owner.Name FROM Opportunity, what does Owner represent?
options: The relationship from the Account to the User who owns it
A subquery against the Owner object
A custom field on Opportunity
The name of the Opportunity's stage
questions.explain: Each name before the final field is a relationship: Account goes from Opportunity to Account, Owner goes from Account to its owning User, and Name is the field on that User.

questions.q: How many levels of child-to-parent relationships can a single SOQL query traverse?
options: Up to five
Only one
Up to fifty
There is no limit
questions.explain: SOQL allows at most five levels of child-to-parent traversal in one query; going past that is rejected.

questions.q: What is the relationship name for the standard lookup field OwnerId?
options: Owner
OwnerId__r
Owner__c
OwnerId.Name
questions.explain: For standard lookups the relationship name is the field name without the trailing Id, so OwnerId becomes Owner. For custom lookups, __c becomes __r.

questions.q: An Opportunity has no Account, and your query selects Account.Owner.Name. What happens for that record?
options: The record is returned and the chained field is null
The whole query fails with an error
The record is silently dropped from the results
SOQL substitutes the current user's name
questions.explain: An empty link in the chain gives a null value at the end, similar to a T-SQL LEFT JOIN. The record is not dropped.

questions.q: Which of these is a sensible response when a query would need more than five levels of parent traversal?
options: Restructure by querying an intermediate object directly or running two queries
Add more parentheses around the chain
Replace the dots with underscores
Use SELECT * to get every parent field
questions.explain: The limit is enforced by the platform, so the fix is restructuring the query, not tweaking syntax. SOQL has no SELECT * anyway.
